channel.title: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more" - I want to create a Twitch Channel based on a SCP Article

item.title: Re: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
item.content:encoded:
Thank you so much for the feedback! I really do appreciate the reality check!

I have worked on the concept hoping and waiting to be greenlit, but the legality and licensing of it came into question, so I was trying to get some of it ironed out before continuing. but it has since kind of gotten further out of hand than i had originally intended at this point.

I do plan on starting the twitch channel either way, but in trying to come up with an interesting character for that, i loved the idea of tying it into one of my favorite universe (SCP). Yet so far i have mostly received backlash from the licensing team and others. maybe it won't work after all, but i would still like to test the waters a little deeper before i draw that conclusion.

item.title: Re: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
item.content:encoded:
First and foremost, this is my opinion as one writer to another. Although I am a member of SCPWiki staff I am not speaking to you in any way shape or form as a member of staff. This is just two people talking writing.

As respectfully as possible, this is a tremendous amount of labor and thought-process to undertake for something you have barely begun drafting. The types of minutia you're looking to hammer out could disappear like a puff of smoke in the wind if you fall at writing the underlying SCP.

While I am not a member of the licensing team and do not have any formal opinions or recommendations regarding licensing, I do have several years experiencing on the site including providing feedback and writing successful articles.

You're going to look and feel very silly if you go to all this trouble for something that is summarily deleted. Do not put the cart before the horse with dreams of a smash hit SCP and your own cult Twitch following that blooms from it.

Dreaming big and having ambitions are wonderful, and I hope you have a chance to stare down your goals in life and go for it one day. But dreams are also built upon the little steps along the way. You have no twitch channel if you have no article. Write it first. Make it good. Make it great. Then maybe we can talk about this.

If you cannot see one existing without the other, then that's all the more reason to step back and reconsider what you're doing.

item.title: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I recently came up with an idea for a SCP Article and Concept that I don't think has ever been done before and isn't really covered in the wiki's legal guidelines.

Essentially I want to create a VTuber (Virtual YouTuber or Twitch Streamer) to stream on Twitch with. VTuber's are generally 3D models that are rigged to react to the operator's movements and emotions. I wanted to create one based off of a SCP article (That i am currently writing) which would be useed as his backstory.

For more information on the Concept: VTuber SCP Concept

So…. I have a lot of questions…

+ show block
– hide block

Questions about Twitch Licensing and Credits:
1. Since the Character I would be streaming as is based on a SCP Article which falls under SCPwiki’s CC Licensing, I would assume the content I produce would need to fall under that same License? If so, I'm not sure how to set that up with twitch as I'm not entirely sure what their content falls under.

2. With the Character being an original creation of mine, would I still need to link to it’s article page and the Author (Me) for credit? Or would just linking to the SCPwiki be sufficient?

3. What rules and/or limitations (if any) would I need to abide by in my content since twitch is an Offsite platform? Examples: 1. Would I be able to stream myself as this character playing a game? even though the game may fall under a different license than CC? 2. As a musician, would I be able to cover copyrighted songs? (provided I follow twitch’s guidelines concerning music as well)

Questions about the Model:
I created the Model and Name before I had the idea to make it a SCP. In that case, would the model (including related images) and name still belong to me, but just be used on the wiki and on stream with my permission? Or would the model and name need to be under CC as well?

Not all of the content being producing would be directly related to the SCP universe, but if the character is connected, I'm not sure what limitations and restrictions would be applied

I love the SCP Universe and don't want to do anything that would be against their guidelines, nor do I want to incur the wrath of a DMCA Take down.

In closing I have no idea what I am doing lol, and any legal help or advice is extremely appreciated!

(There are probably many things that I have not thought of and many questions may rise up. if you have any questions or suggestions of other questions I should be asking, please let me know)
